newsitem.title: GERMANY: European feeds buyers active for winter months.
newsitem.headline: European feeds buyers active for winter months.

text.p: European feed makers are buying raw material for winter shipment now that forecasts of a higher than expected U.S. soybean crop have reduced prices, grain trader Toepfer said in a newsletter.
The October 11 soy forecast shaved $10 per tonne off Latin American soymeal prices in Rotterdam this week.
Toepfer said Chinese spot soymeal buying in the U.S. had spurred European buyers, as had the fact that Latin American old crop supplies were set to run out.
A market report by the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) said buying focused on nearby months only.

Soymeal demand rose as crushers were unable or unwilling to secure expensive domestic rapeseed from a much reduced 1996 harvest, ASA said, but noted that relatively cheap Latin American sun pellets were competing with other nearby protein feeds.
Toepfer reported brisk nearby demand for corngluten, tapioca, cane molasses and citrus pellets.
Prices of palmkernel cake and copra products firmed on brisk demand but were expected to ease in the fourth quarter amid origin supply pressure, it said.
Consumers needed more fishmeal cover but little was available from Peru and Chile because of fishing bans, which should underpin prices.
Peruvian fishmeal over the past month had risen $20 cif northern Europe to $620.
